items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: I used to get a big kick out of Peter Davis, you know, the one that played and taught Louie. ... Peter Davis was working out there too, and he was teaching the band too, see. And somebody wrote a book and it said that Jones taught Louie how to play the cornet, see. And Manny would come around the st

ctx.x: And after the Jazz Band, the original Dixieland Jazz Band made these recordings, then he eliminated the test, see, and anybody could come in then, you see. No, the musicians union in them days, those fellas were all artists, you know. It was a different breed, different breed of musicians, and a happy-go-lucky type, you know. And they were serious musicians, very serious. And like the other guys, you know, they were all, they had a lot of bands that played good, you know, of course, talk about, well, Jules played…
Louie Armstrong and all these different musicians, but did you ever play the banjo? I know you used to sell banjo mutes. They talk about that. Yeah. You kept all different kind of accessories, huh?
In my store you could get anything you wanted, see. You see, Dick, here's the dip. You got this on and on?
